alerts.title: Acute Kidney Injury with TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines state that intercurrent illnesses with dehydration may cause renal function deterioration in patients on TDF, requiring creatinine checks during hospital admission. The patient has severe gastroenteritis with dehydration (dry mucous membranes, sunken eyes, low BP) and an acute creatinine rise from 0.9 to 2.4 mg/dL. The urea-to-creatinine ratio of 24:1 and low sodium/potassium suggest prerenal AKI from dehydration. TDF is a potential nephrotoxin, but the clinical picture strongly supports dehydration as the primary cause.

evidence.recommended_action: Manage dehydration with IV fluids as planned. Re-evaluate TDF continuation after AKI resolves, considering guideline alternatives like ABC+3TC+DTG.

alerts.title: Consider TDF Switch Post-AKI
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend ABC+3TC+DTG as an alternative regimen if renal impairment develops due to TDF. The clinician is considering stopping TDF permanently due to AKI. The current AKI is likely prerenal, but a permanent switch may be warranted if renal impairment persists after rehydration. The plan to stop TDF aligns with guidelines if the impairment is attributed to the drug.

evidence.recommended_action: After treating dehydration, reassess renal function. If eGFR remains <50 mL/min/1.73m², switch to ABC+3TC+DTG per guidelines.

alerts.title: Missing Routine Creatinine Monitoring
alerts.message: Guidelines advise checking creatinine in patients on TDF during intercurrent illness with dehydration. The patient was on TDF for 2 years, with the last creatinine check 375 days ago. Routine monitoring prior to this acute illness was overdue. The current severe dehydration necessitated the check, revealing AKI.

evidence.recommended_action: Ensure creatinine is monitored during this admission and schedule regular renal function tests per ART monitoring guidelines after recovery.
